standard_prerequisites.name: Infinite sums and rational equivalence
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter chow.tex, label remark-infinite-sums-rational-equivalences, invoked at proof line 5688
standard_prerequisites.use: Justifies replacing a locally finite sum of pulled back cycles by the pullback of the sum, which is the first reduction of the proof.

standard_prerequisites.name: Exactness of the sequence of an open immersion
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter chow.tex, labels lemma-restrict-to-open (proof line 5705) and lemma-exact-sequence-open (proof line 5700)
standard_prerequisites.use: Lets a cycle on the closed complement be extended to a cycle on Y and identifies the kernel of restriction, which is what makes the induction on the dimension of Y work.

core_obligations: Reduce to a single dominant integral cycle: write alpha as a locally finite sum of integral components W_j, let Z_j be the closure of f(W_j), and observe both that the Z_j form a locally finite family and that it suffices to handle [W] on f^{-1}(Z_j) separately (proof lines 5662-5692).

Induct on d = dim_delta(Y): if d < k there is nothing to prove, otherwise use the product structure over a dense open V to write the restriction of alpha as a pullback, extend the resulting cycle from V to Y, and push the difference into the complement of V, whose dimension is smaller (proof lines 5694-5709).

Finish in the case X = Y times A^r: factor the projection into r successive projections with fibre A^1, reduce further to r = 1 and to a dominant integral W, and split into the case W = Y times A^1, where [W] = f^*[Y], and the case of a proper inclusion, where the generic fibre of W over Y is cut out by a monic irreducible polynomial whose coefficients spread out over a nonempty open V, so that alpha restricted to f^{-1}(V) is rationally trivial and induction on the dimension of Y applies again (proof lines 5711-5733).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to one integral dominating cycle over an integral base (proof lines 5662-5692).
Induct on the dimension of the base using the product structure over a dense open and the exact sequence of the open immersion (proof lines 5694-5709).
Reduce to the A^1 case and conclude by the polynomial description of the generic fibre (proof lines 5711-5733).
difficulty_reason: The lemma says that pullback along a flat morphism of relative dimension r which is locally a product with A^r over the base is surjective on Chow groups in every degree (statement lines 5650-5660, tag 02TT). The proof is a genuine induction on two parameters: on the dimension of the base, using the product structure over a dense open together with the exact sequence of an open immersion, and then on the number r of A^1 factors, where the remaining case is that of a dominant integral hypersurface whose generic fibre is cut out by a monic irreducible polynomial, giving rational triviality after shrinking the base. Both reductions require the reader to track cycles through open immersions and infinite sums, so the claim is H2.
